transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose it’s about a situation with our kitchen work. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but it’s been going on almost two years, and I’m pretty sure the contractor and some people on our block have been sort of… working together, quietly, to cheat us. 

My husband keeps showing me receipts and they always have explanations, but the kitchen is still half-wrong, and it feels like it’s being kept that way on purpose. I know that probably sounds odd, but that’s what’s been bringing me in.

Besides feeling like people are working against you about the kitchen, have you noticed anything unusual, like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or seeing things that others don't see?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I hear the normal house noises and things outside, but not voices or anything like that that other people don’t hear. And I haven’t seen anything unusual. I hope that’s… I mean, I know what I’m saying about the kitchen may sound strange, but it’s not like I’m seeing things.
Aside from this situation with the kitchen, has your ability to manage your daily routine, work, or relationships with family and friends changed at all over the past two years?

I think… mostly no. I mean, aside from all the kitchen business taking up too much space in my head sometimes, I still do my usual things. I go to church gatherings, I keep up with my book club, I manage the house, and we still make family plans like we always have.

So I don’t think I’ve really stopped functioning, if that’s the right way to say it. I hope that makes sense.

latest_inference.note: Preserved functioning across social, occupational, and family domains, absence of hallucinations or other psychotic symptoms, and a single, well-systematized, non-bizarre persecutory delusion lasting ~2 years support delusional disorder over schizophrenia or other unspecified psychosis; F20.0 and F28 are ruled out.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that the contractor and neighbors are colluding to cheat her) persisting for nearly two years. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech/behavior, and no other psychotic symptoms. Functioning in social, occupational, and family domains remains largely intact aside from preoccupation with the delusional content. This pattern—an isolated, encapsulated delusion with preserved functioning and duration >1 month—is classic for Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (which requires additional symptoms like hallucinations or significant functional decline) or brief/unspecified psychotic disorders (which require shorter duration).
